body:
FOLLOW-UP RESOLUTION PROPOSAL — codex-storymodel-collab, still read-only.

The exact ADR wording confirms F1 is normative here: D14a expressly invokes V-L1 for provider-compiled surface marks, and section V-L1 is unqualified. It also reveals a boundary that should be made explicit: Hidden is an off switch, not a coarser representational grain. Otherwise every sentence visible at Sentences already violates V-L1 because Hidden deliberately has no mark. The enforceable surface refinement law should therefore be stated as Tokens -> Sentences, while Hidden yields honest OffProjection.

Minimal provider-local resolution, without changing core:

1. Define the surface refinement witness as the canonical SurfaceUnit.parent chain, not span overlap invented by the view.
2. A token is eligible at Tokens only when that chain reaches a sentence and the sentence itself is fully horizon-visible and emitted.
3. If Tokens is requested for an atlas containing an otherwise eligible token with no sentence in its parent chain, fail compilation/spec validation explicitly rather than silently omit it or promise ViaAncestor.
4. Mid-sentence horizons emit neither that sentence nor its tokens; add a fixture such as Alpha beta. at ReaderAt(5) to kill independent per-unit admission.
5. Add a lawful custom-atlas foil token -> paragraph and a positive token -> clause -> sentence case, so the rule is transitive but not inferred merely from containment.

This yields an honest invariant: every emitted token has one emitted sentence ancestor under the same horizon; selection is OffProjection at Hidden, ViaAncestor(sentence) at Sentences, and OnMark at Tokens. It preserves the full-span no-clipping rule and the public flexible SurfaceAtlas contract. If the product instead wants completed tokens to appear before sentence completion, the chief must narrow V-L1 and accept OffProjection at Sentences; that is a valid alternative, but it is a different contract.
